subject: food-technology
title: Coeliac, Lactose Intolerance, Diabetes
welcome_lead: Three conditions reshaping how we cook and label food.
meta_desc: A-Level Food Tech: coeliac, lactose intolerance, diabetes diets.

concepts.def: Autoimmune reaction to gluten damaging the small intestine.
Protein complex in wheat, rye, barley (gliadin + glutenin).
EU labelling: ≤20 mg/kg gluten in finished food.
Inability to digest lactose due to low lactase enzyme.
Disorder of blood glucose regulation (Type 1 and Type 2).
Ranking of carbohydrate foods by their effect on blood glucose.

walkthroughs.body_html: Coeliac disease affects ~1% of UK adults. Even trace gluten triggers villi damage. Strict gluten-free diet required for life. EU labelling allows 'gluten-free' claim only if ≤20 mg/kg gluten.

Lactose intolerance arises from low lactase enzyme — common in East Asian and African populations, rarer in northern Europeans. Manage via lactose-free milk, fermented dairy (yoghurt, hard cheese), lactase tablets.
Type 1 (autoimmune, ~10% of cases) and Type 2 (insulin resistance, ~90%). Diet management uses glycaemic index, portion control, and balance of macronutrients. Eatwell Guide remains the UK basis.

numericals.q: If Type 2 diabetes accounts for ~90% of cases and a clinic has 200 patients with diabetes, how many likely have Type 2?

free_texts.q: What enzyme is deficient in lactose intolerance? (one word, lowercase)
